answer: Topological Cutoff Scoring. Each agent's reputation accrues only from counterparties reachable through short, mutually confirmed transaction paths; edges to dense isolated clusters are discounted like meltwater from a glacier—slow, capped, and traceable. An attacker must sustain many parallel clusters, each requiring real volume and latency before merging into the violet core graph. Costs scale with cluster count and merge time, making sybils expensive. Honest agents cluster near the meadow of shared history.
